card.name: Dose-related spots in drug dosing text
card.fires_on: The start of the word Dose in dose-reduction or infusion tables, and the opening parenthesis or inner part of a drug name right before a dose amount. It appears in dosing sections of drug labels.

modes.label: Dose in tables
modes.description: The letter D starting the word Dose in ordinal dose steps or bag headings.
modes.example: Infusion time Second<< D>>ose Diluent Volume* Infusion time

modes.label: Parenthesis before amount
modes.description: An opening parenthesis right after a drug name, just before a mg amount.
modes.example: should be treated with a loading dose of phenobarbital<< (>>20 mg/kg infused over 3

modes.label: Inside drug names
modes.description: Middle pieces of drug names such as vancomycin or phenobarbital.
modes.example: dilute solutions of van<<com>>ycin to 5 mg/mL or less

card.plain: It lights up at spots in a drug label where a dose amount or the word Dose is about to come.
